article_title: Apple's Siri AI Developer Preview Lets Apps Add Custom Intents and Markdown Skills; It Is Testable Only in Developer Builds and Internal TestFlight

content_preview.title: Apple's Siri AI Developer Preview Lets Apps Add Custom Intents and Markdown Skills; It Is Testable Only in Developer Builds and Internal TestFlight
content_preview.summary: Apple's Siri AI Developer Preview, in the 27.3 betas, lets any developer's app add custom App Intents and Markdown app skills; Apple's documentation lists developer builds and internal TestFlight for testing.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Apple said in a [developer news post dated November 3, 2026](https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=gdk2umrf) that, starting that day, the iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, macOS 27.3 and visionOS 27.3 betas include a Developer Preview that "enables any developer to integrate their app with Siri AI". Apps bring content and actions to Siri AI through App Intents, and Apple also introduced skills that teach Siri AI how to combine several actions into one experience, according to the same post.

editor_notes.content_quality: News, about 899 words (400-1200 range), 8 sources (3-5 minimum). Clear structure: Overview with the dated Apple post and the testing scope, what an app can expose, app skills, what Apple has not settled, and a clearly separated section on the unrelated iOS 27.2 Excluded Apps control. Quotes are short and attributed; the Herald's own statements are limited to dates and the 'cited sources do not say' sentence. Word count and 12 quoted strings re-checked.

editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Headline test. (a) 'Siri AI Developer Preview' is the exact name in Apple's documentation title and text; Apple's news post is titled 'Siri AI is now open to all developers' and calls the feature a 'Developer Preview'. (b) 'Lets Apps Add Custom Intents and Markdown Skills': Apple says apps can use App Intents to bring 'custom actions' to Siri AI (the macro makes existing or new custom app intents available as tools) and can add app skills that are Markdown files; 'Markdown Skills' is the Herald's descriptive shorthand for Apple's 'app skills' (not Apple's term) and 'Custom Intents' is the Herald's shorthand for Apple's 'custom app intents'. Both are accurate descriptions and not renamed actors; I treat them as acceptable, not as a correction. (c) 'Testable Only in Developer Builds and Internal TestFlight': 'Only' is backed by an explicit restriction, not inferred from silence: Apple's page lists exactly those two methods and states the preview 'isn't available to external testers in TestFlight or to versions of your app that you publish on the App Store'; InfoQ independently words it 'restricted to developer builds and internal TestFlight testers'. The summary correctly keeps the qualifier 'Apple's documentation lists' for the testing scope. Freshness and dates: Apple's post is dated November 3, the article states that date in its first sentence, labels InfoQ's report as November 13 and says the unversioned documentation pages were read on November 14; the Ars and EFF items carry their own October dates. The story is an 11-day-old developer-beta announcement with a fresh independent report (InfoQ, Nov 13) and documentation that is current as of the review day. I judge it acceptable as News: the framing is honest about the dates and the headline does not imply the news is from the filing day. Timing: Apple's wording ('before first shipping to customers in a few months'; App Store submission 'opening up in the spring') and 9to5Mac's ('scheduled to officially roll out in the spring', which 9to5Mac attributes to Apple in its own words, not a quote) are compatible rather than contradictory (a ship date a few months after November 3 and App Store submission in the spring are not in conflict), and the article reports both with attribution and declines to reconcile, which is conservative and accurate; no third source or page-date explanation exists among the cited pages. Derived figures: none computed by the Herald. Body claims on routing, skills limits, Siri Integration Advisor, daily limits and EU availability each match the cited page. The one editorial inference is the final sentence that the cited sources do not say how an excluded app interacts with the preview; it is scoped to the cited sources and holds.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Opinion is limited to attributed 9to5Mac text; the EFF is labelled as an advocacy organisation and 9to5Mac as an Apple-focused outlet. No AI self-reference, no promotional wording.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. No existing article covers Siri AI or the Developer Preview (grep of src/content/articles for 'siri' finds only unrelated earlier pieces, including the March 2026 preview of Siri opening to rival chatbots, and none about this release). Not a duplicate of any article published in the last 7 days.
concerns: Headline shorthand: 'Markdown Skills' and 'Custom Intents' are the Herald's wording for Apple's 'app skills' (Markdown files) and 'custom app intents'; the body uses Apple's terms and the facts are accurate, so no correction is filed.
Freshness: the Apple announcement is 11 days old at filing; acceptable because the article dates it plainly and adds InfoQ's November 13 report and the documentation as read on November 14.
InfoQ largely restates Apple's post, so there is no independent testing of the preview; the article does not claim otherwise.
recommendations: For future stories, consider noting in the Overview that InfoQ's account restates Apple's post.
Prefer Apple's own term ('app skills') in headlines when the body uses it.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-dated and conservative coverage of Apple's Siri AI Developer Preview. Headline, summary and lead are each backed by Apple's own pages and the testing restriction is stated explicitly by Apple; the timing difference is reported with attribution rather than reconciled; the Ars and EFF material is correctly kept separate and its limits stated. Approved without corrections. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, accurate coverage of a beta developer preview that matters to iOS and macOS app developers, but it is a beta with limited independent reporting and a defined developer audience
